name: retype-xp-backend
title: Per-answer XP computed by the shared grader (matches the web's values), with requeue 3 and retype 2
issue: User decision 2026-10-10, for web issue EpicNicks/Qamooscheh-Web#44 and the XP drift found between web and backend. TODAY: XpPolicy.ForSession sums per-lexeme FSRS-grade awards (Again 0 / Hard 8 / Good 10 / Easy 15) over the collapsed first-attempt review_log entries; the web shows a cosmetic per-answer burst from E:/Code/Projects/Qamooscheh-Web/Qamooscheh-Web/src/domain/xp.ts (xpForAnswer: +10 correct, +7 accepted with a typo, +5 correct on a retry, half when hinted). NEW MODEL: (1) XP is per answered exercise attempt, computed by ONE function in the shared grader that clients already load (the Qamooscheh grader and its Browser/Wasi shims; see tools/README.md), so web, Android and server compute identical numbers and clients just display the returned value. (2) Values: port xpForAnswer exactly from the web's src/domain/xp.ts (read it; keep its rounding and hint rule) with two changes: a correct answer on a requeued/later attempt of a missed exercise earns 3 (not 5), and a correct RETYPE earns 2. Answer speed is ignored. Practice rounds are never submitted and earn nothing (unchanged). (3) RETYPE: after a wrong typed answer the client may let the learner retype the correct answer once (optional 'Retry' button). The grader grades the retype (same comparison as the exercise) and returns its XP. Add an optional field on the submitted wrong attempt carrying the retype text or result so the server re-grades and credits it; credit only an attempt graded wrong of a typed render type, at most once; it never changes grading, FSRS reviews or completion. (4) Server: session XP (lesson sessions and checkpoints, which use XpPolicy today) becomes the sum of the grader's per-attempt XP over the submitted attempts, re-computed server-side (never trust a client number). FSRS grading, review_log and GradeMapper stay exactly as they are; only XP changes. Flashcard XP is unchanged. Idempotent resubmission must not double-count. (5) The submit and checkpoint responses return the session's XP total (and per-attempt XP if cheap) so clients can show the real number. (6) Old clients keep working (new fields optional). (7) Tests: the XP function's table (each case), retype validation, requeue, hinted, server total equals the sum, checkpoint, idempotency. (8) Rebuild/publish the grader shims the way tools/README.md says if they are checked in or versioned, and expose the XP function in the browser shim's exports. (9) Update API_SPEC.md (XP section, submit/checkpoint bodies and responses, the grader's exported API) and add features.yaml entry 'per-answer-xp' (backend: implemented, web: not_yet, android: not_yet). If the grader cannot host this function for a reason the plan doesn't cover, stop with needsUser.
acceptance: One grader XP function used by the server, exported to clients
Values match web xp.ts except requeue 3 and retype 2; speed ignored
FSRS/review_log unchanged; dotnet build and test green locally and in CI
